text: Immuno-oncology, the first broadly successful strategy for metastatic cancer, must be integrated with chemotherapy, radiation and targeted small molecules. Immunotherapy was initially perceived as less toxic, but as it becomes first- and second-line treatment, immunotoxicity and autoimmunity are emerging as its Achilles' heel; notably, immunotoxicity appears to bode well for the patient. Separately, combining DNA methyltransferase inhibitors (DNMTis) with histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACis) yields a new low-dose sequential regimen with robust anti-tumour effect in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In treated NSCLC cell lines, an interferon α/β transcriptional program upregulates antigen presentation via double-stranded RNA induction, suppresses MYC signaling and increases T cell chemoattractant CCL5; in mouse models it reverses tumour immune evasion and shifts T cell exhaustion toward memory/effector phenotypes. Finally, ~twofold reduced interleukin-2 (IL-2) expression underlies Idd3-linked autoimmune susceptibility, impairing CD4+ CD25+ regulatory T cell function.
